title: WHAT IF YOU WENT BACK TO 2010 WITH $100?

segments.line: He leaves his card on the table.
It just has a phone number. And a date.
The twentieth of June.
That night, you hear Mum on the phone in the kitchen. She's crying. The
bank is taking the house.
You remember now. You were too little to understand it the first time, but this is the summer you had to move.
In 2010 alone, banks in America took more than a million homes. That's real.
The man's offer would save the house. Tonight.
But you'd lose everything those coins will become.
Mo says keep them. 'He wouldn't want them if they weren't worth it. '
Ellie climbs onto your bed with her teddy, Captain Buttons. 'Are we moving? ' she asks.
And then you remember.
The crash comes on the nineteenth of June. That's why his date is the twentieth.
He wants the coins after the crash, when you're scared, and they look worthless.
But you also remember the rule. Sell too much, and you change the future. Then nothing you remember is true anymore.
So you sell just enough.
On the eighth of June, at thirty dollars a coin, you sell two thousand bitcoins.
Sixty thousand dollars.
You give it to Mum in an envelope.
She asks where it came from. You say, 'Pizza. '
The house is saved.
You keep eight thousand coins.
You write the password on a piece of paper, fold it small, and
sew it inside Captain Buttons.
When the man calls on the twentieth, you don't pick up.
